positives: If this company sold everything it owns and paid off everything it owes, there would be real money left over. It owns more than it owes.
worries: The profit behind each share of stock has actually been shrinking over the last few years, not growing.
Using simple math based on its profit and what it owns, the stock looks priced above what the business is roughly worth - you'd be paying more than the simple math says it's worth.

qualitative.filing_summary_10k: For fiscal 2026 (ended January 31, 2026), Best Buy reported revenue of $41.7 billion, up 0.4%, with comparable sales growth of 0.5% driven by computing and mobile phones, partially offset by declines in home theater and appliances. Operating income rose to $1,389 million from $1,262 million, aided by lower goodwill/intangible impairments, though restructuring charges increased due to a labor and store optimization initiative and a Best Buy Health restructuring; the filing also flags ongoing tariff uncertainty following a Supreme Court ruling on IEEPA tariffs. Total store count fell to 1,068 from 1,125 two years earlier, and the company continued scaling newer initiatives like Best Buy Ads and Best Buy Marketplace.
qualitative.filing_summary_10q: The most recent 10-Q (for the quarter ended August 1, 2026, fiscal Q2 2027) is provided only as raw XBRL data without narrative text. The tags indicate continued restructuring activity across a fiscal 2026 labor and store optimization initiative, a Best Buy Health optimization and China sourcing initiative, and a 2024 resource optimization initiative, as well as a subsequent event related to an IEEPA tariff refund disclosed after quarter-end. qualitative.filing_summary_8k: This Form 8-K, dated August 27, 2026, discloses under Item 2.02 that Best Buy issued a news release announcing results of operations for the second quarter ended August 1, 2026, and held an earnings conference call the same day. The release is furnished as Exhibit 99 and is not deemed 'filed' for liability purposes under the Exchange Act. qualitative.moat_explanation: The excerpts describe Best Buy as operating in a highly competitive, price-conscious retail sector where it explicitly maintains price-matching policies and states its higher-cost service model 'creates additional margin pressure' versus lower-cost competitors. It has no long-term supplier contracts and depends heavily on a handful of vendors (five suppliers ~55% of purchases), which undercuts claims of a durable structural advantage; the cited 'competitive advantages' (stores, staff, vendor partnerships) are asserted but not shown to be difficult for rivals to replicate.
red_flags: Vendor concentration: 20 largest suppliers ~80% of merchandise purchased, with five suppliers (Apple, Samsung, HP, LG, Sony) ~55% of total purchases, and no long-term contracts securing supply terms
Goodwill and intangible asset impairments at Best Buy Health tied to a customer base change and pressures in Medicaid/Medicare Advantage markets
Management acknowledges a higher cost structure than some competitors, creating margin pressure
Ongoing tariff and trade policy uncertainty (IEEPA tariffs ruled unauthorized by the Supreme Court, with unresolved refund process) affecting cost structure
Net store count decline (1,068 stores vs. 1,125 two years prior) alongside restructuring initiatives involving labor and store optimization
Comparable sales declines in appliances and consumer electronics/home theater categories in the most recent fiscal year
